rv.q: But I'm afraid that this is in many respects an inadequate account of the part.
Sheridan Smith makes for one hell of a bitch.
While this may not be the best Hedda Gabler that you could ever see, it effortlessly holds the attention for three hours, mainly through comedy.
But she's never fully commanding as a woman seizing her own destiny after that tedious honeymoon with George Tesman.
But in this richly intelligent performance, Smith conveys Hedda’s material ambition, her boredom and her deluded romantic idealism.

cn.t: Mixed reviews for this production, with critics finding Brian Friel's modern adaptation lively and fun, but Sheridan Smith's casting as the chilly antiheroine proving divisive and ultimately unconvincing for some.
